- uri (required): The URI of the resource to read

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

summary.description: One-sentence statement of the defect

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

args.description: Optional arguments for the skill

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: WaitForMcpServers
tools.description:
Wait for MCP servers that are still connecting and whose tools are not
yet in your tool list. Pass `servers` to wait for specific ones, or omit
it to wait for all pending servers (once none is pending, a call without
`servers` reports any server that failed to connect or is not configured).

If the user's request needs tools from a still-connecting server, call this
tool to wait for it. Once it connects, its tools will be added to your tool
list and you can use them directly. Returns ready=true when servers are
ready, ready=false if they failed to connect, need authentication, or are
disabled.

You do not need to ask the user for confirmation to use this tool.

servers.description: Server names to wait for (default: all pending)

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool.   export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>

        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )

  return { confirmed }

Contents of /home/yu/projects/dsh-agent-team/.scratch/AGENTS.md:

# .scratch Work Rules

This subtree holds cross-session work items: design snapshots, research, implementation tickets, prototypes, and acceptance evidence. It is not an implementation or API authority — current behavior is defined by `packages/` source and tests, and maintenance rules by [`../docs/AGENTS.md`](../docs/AGENTS.md). This file only governs how to work here.

## Work-item structure

Each `active/<work>/` is one directory with a short `README.md` as its single continuation entry, covering five items: status, last-checked date, current frontier (who is doing what and what is blocked), completion conditions, and the formal-doc exit.

```
active/<work>/
├── README.md      # continuation entry (the five items above)
├── spec.md        # confirmed decision snapshot — written once discussion converges
├── issues/        # tracer-bullet implementation tickets, one file per ticket
│   ├── 01-<slug>.md
│   └── 02-<slug>.md
├── materials/     # research and external material (keep only what is worth re-reading)
└── validation/    # human-confirmed acceptance evidence (see the development doc)
```

## Ticket discipline

Each `issues/NN-<slug>.md` uses a fixed skeleton, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first):

```markdown
# NN — title

**What to build:** the end-to-end behavior this ticket demonstrably delivers once done (user perspective, not a layered task list)
**Blocked by:** the tickets blocking it, or "None — can start immediately"
**Status:** pending | ready | in-progress | complete

- [ ] acceptance criterion 1
- [ ] acceptance criterion 2
```

- **Vertical slices**: each ticket cuts one narrow, complete path through every layer (schema → API → UI → tests), independently verifiable when done; no horizontal division of labor by layer.
- **Self-contained tickets**: each ticket can start in a new context without reading the whole work-item history. Avoid concrete file paths and code snippets (they go stale); exception: decision-dense fragments from prototypes (state machines, type shapes) may be inlined with their source noted.
- **Frontier workflow**: tickets whose blockers are all done form the frontier and are ready to start; a serial chain runs top to bottom. Tickets that are written but still carry unfinished blockers stay **pending**, so `ready` always means startable now.
- **Wide-refactor exception**: when one mechanical change's blast radius covers the whole repository, do not force it into a tracer bullet — order it as expand–contract: expand first (old and new coexist), migrate in batches, then contract (delete the old form).

## Lifecycle

- **Closing a work item**: close or delete unfinished tickets → move durable conclusions into the `../docs/` maintained documents → delete process material without provenance value → move into `archive/YYYY-MM/`.
- **Archive is history**: archived states and terminology only represent the working context of their time and never override current implementation; do not rewrite archives to match new code.
- **Transient artifacts**: logs, debug screenshots, and downloads go in `local/` or `artifacts/` (gitignored), never into active or archive.

## Version control

- **Active does not enter version history**: while a work item is open, its `active/<work>/` directory is gitignored working material. Force-add it (`git add -f`) only when a reviewer must see it.
- **Archive enters history on close**: when a work item closes, move it into `archive/YYYY-MM/` and amend that move into the commit(s) that deliver the work, so the archive records what actually shipped instead of sitting in a scratch-only commit at the tip.

## Directory index

See [README.md](README.md).

1	# Review 01 — attention-delivery-model
2	
3	**Conclusion:** Changes needed
4	**Work item:** attention-delivery-model
5	**Ticket:** Whole work item (tickets 01–05, all marked complete)
6	**Compared:** `6f2ca5a..HEAD` (`7558dfd`)
7	**Commits:** `7761537`, `f821206`, `51f58d8`, `8a27985`, `7558dfd`
8	**Reviewed:** 2026-10-28
9	
10	三个独立评审轴（spec / correctness / standards）并行运行，候选发现经逐条复核后汇总。每条结论都有可复现的输入或代码路径支撑；不可复现的列入「未验证范围」。
11	
12	## Findings
13	
14	### blocker — Main stream 读取回放校验拒绝当前格式的记录，账本无法重开
15	
16	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:6292`（`repairLegacyMainStreamRead`），入口 `:6255`
17	
18	**现象：** `prepareMainReadFrom` 只在读取真正推进 watermark 时才写 `inbox.mainAttention` 行。一次只消费 marker、不推进水位的 Agent 读取，存的是「只有 marker」的 inbox。`repairLegacyMainStreamRead` 无法把这条当前格式的记录与 Attention 之前的旧凭据区分开，于是给它补了一行 Attention；`validateOperation`（`:3212`）随后按当前格式重新推导出 `advances === false`，期待「只有 marker」的 inbox，两者不符，抛 `invalid Main stream read receipt`。构造函数会 replay 并 validate，因此之后每次启动 Host 都失败。
19	
20	**复现（实测）：** Agent 在 follow 之前被 Human 在 Main stream @（seq 7）→ `team_attention projectRef follow`（start 8，readThrough 7）→ `team_thread read projectRef`（默认 readThrough = head 7）。读取提交成功（消费 1 个 marker，`advances=false`），随后 `new AgentTeamLedger(table, …)` 抛错。这条路径就是 `main-stream.spec.ts:376` 已经测过的「先被 mention、再 follow、再读」流程，只是那个测试没有重开账本。
21	
22	**依据：** 修复回归本身。本工作项的验收缝 9 要求「重放校验覆盖迁移后的持久表示」；上一轮修复（`7558dfd`）解决了旧账本打不开，却让新写入的合法记录也打不开。
23	
24	**最小修复：** 只在当前构建本该写出一行时才修——先算 `this.prepareMainReadFrom(projection, memberId, projectRef, readThroughSequence)`，`!prepared.advances` 时直接 `return operation`。这同时覆盖「readThrough 低于 Attention 起点」的旧部分读取。
25	
26	---
27	
28	### major — 非 owner 的 Main stream follower 永远收不到唤醒
29	
30	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:2708-2739`（`affectedMembersOf`）
31	
32	**现象：** 普通 Main 工作的唤醒名单来自 Project owner（`:2731-2737`）、发送者和 Main marker。非 owner Member 的 `mainAttention` 行不出现在名单的任何来源里，而 `touchedThreadRefs` 对 `team/main-message-posted` 不返回 Thread。结果是 follower 的 `standing.unreadCount` 在涨，Host 却从未对它调用 `notifyMember`。
33	
34	**复现（Host 级实测）：** 非 owner Member follow Project Main → Human 发一条 Main 消息，follower `unreadCount: 1`、唤醒调用 0 次；Human 开一个 discussion，`unreadCount: 2`、唤醒 0 次。反向同样断裂：follower 发言时 `affectedMembersOf` 只返回 `["member:f1"]`，Human owner 不在名单里（Human 的 Main 未读靠派生，本就不在 `projectOwnerIds` 中）。
35	
36	**依据：** `docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md` 声明 Main stream 普通更新对 Attention 覆盖的读者是 Immediate；`team_attention follow` 的 render 文案是 "Ordinary updates from there will interrupt you"。票据 03 的验收条件要求 owner 与非 owner 在 follow / unfollow / 读取 / **唤醒**上对称。
37	
38	**最小修复：** 对每个追加 Main source 的操作（`team/main-message-posted`、discussion 形态的 `team/thread-started`、`team/project-owner-added/removed`），把该 Project 下持有 Main attention 行、且不是发送者的 Member 加入名单。**必须先做下一条 membership 门禁**，否则这会把 Main 内容投给非成员。
39	
40	---
41	
42	### major — Main stream Attention 的 follow/status 与 Main inbox 行没有 Project 成员门禁
43	
44	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:1756-1762`（`writeMainAttention`）、`:1861-1872`（`mainAttentionStatus`）、`:2014-2031`（`mainInboxItems`）、`:1400-1408`（`mainNotificationFacts`）
45	
46	**现象：** `writeMainAttention` 只校验 Workspace（`assertActorForWorkspace` + `requireActiveProject`），而 `postMainMessage`、`readMainStream`、`mainStreamHistory` 都会调 `requireProjectMemberActor`。Thread 的 inbox 循环有成员门禁（`:1910`），Main 的循环没有。
47	
48	**复现（实测）：** 一个参与 Workspace 但不属于该 Project 的 Member `changeAttention(projectRef, follow)` 成功提交。随后 `memberInbox` 返回一行 Main，`previewText` 是 Project 消息正文的首行（实测取到 `secret project talk`），而 `mainStreamHistory` 对同一个 Member 抛 `not_project_member`。也就是说：读全文被拒，摘要照样泄露。`team_attention projectRef` 让这成为模型的常规动作。
49	
50	**依据：** DESIGN「参与与可见性仍由现有权限模型决定」；`docs/AGENTS.md`「Source and tests define implementation behavior」。
51	
52	**最小修复：** `writeMainAttention` 与 `mainAttentionStatus` 加 `this.requireProjectMemberActor(actor, project.projectRef)`；`mainInboxItems` 与 `mainNotificationFacts` 镜像 Thread 循环的 `isProjectMember` 过滤。**重放校验保持在 `participatesInProjectWorkspaceFrom`**，否则后来被移除成员的历史 follow 无法重放。
53	
54	---
55	
56	### major — owner 授权覆盖已存在的 follow 行，静默清掉未读
57	
58	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:890-894`（写入）与 `:2925-2927`（校验）
59	
60	**现象：** `team/project-owner-added` 无条件把 `startMainAttention(member, project, grantSeq)` 放进 delta，替换掉已有行，`readThroughSequence` 被压成 `grantSeq - 1`。
61	
62	**复现（实测）：** Member follow Main（watermark 1）→ Human 发两条普通更新（unread 2）→ Human 授予 owner 身份，该 Member 的普通未读在没有读取的情况下归 0，存储行的 `readThroughSequence` 跳到授权点。这与「撤回 owner 保留这一行」的对称性相反，也与 `project-owners.spec.ts:107` 的注释「Attention 属于 Member 自己」相反。
63	
64	**依据：** DESIGN「身份撤销不自动收回既有 Attention：此时持续关注可能已经成为 Member 自己的选择」。同一个问题在 Thread 侧不存在——`followAttention` 会拒绝重复建行。
65	
66	**最小修复：** 仅在 `mainAttentionForFrom(projection, memberId, projectRef) === undefined` 时才铸授权行，并在 `validateOperation` 的 `grantedMainAttention` 镜像该条件。本构建已写出的账本含覆盖行为，因此校验需同时接受两种形状，或补一条修复。
67	
68	---
69	
70	### minor — Human 的 Main stream unfollow 提交成功但什么都不做
71	
72	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:1776-1790`、`:4684-4689`
73	
74	**现象：** `humanMainAttentionFrom` 对存在的 Project 总是返回一行，所以 unfollow 分支写下 `removed: []` 并回一个 receipt、不带 `attention`。`mainAttentionStatus` 与 `standing.following` 仍为 true，普通未读继续流动。用新的 requestId 重复 unfollow 可以无限次提交；follow 则被「already following」拒绝。
75	
76	**复现（实测）：** unfollow 提交成功 → 状态仍返回 `attention` → 第二次 unfollow 又提交成功 → follow 被拒。通过公开的 `@Remote('changeAttention')` 可达。派生形式满足「默认 follow」这一条（从 `createdAtSequence` 起算、重放确定），但让 unfollow 不可能，且账本报告成功而不是拒绝请求。

# Review 01 — attention-delivery-model

**Conclusion:** Changes needed
**Work item:** attention-delivery-model
**Ticket:** Whole work item (tickets 01–05, all marked complete)
**Compared:** `6f2ca5a..HEAD` (`7558dfd`)
**Commits:** `7761537`, `f821206`, `51f58d8`, `8a27985`, `7558dfd`
**Reviewed:** 2026-10-28

三个独立评审轴（spec / correctness / standards）并行运行，候选发现经逐条复核后汇总。每条结论都有可复现的输入或代码路径支撑；不可复现的列入「未验证范围」。

## Findings

### blocker — Main stream 读取回放校验拒绝当前格式的记录，账本无法重开

**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:6292`（`repairLegacyMainStreamRead`），入口 `:6255`

**现象：** `prepareMainReadFrom` 只在读取真正推进 watermark 时才写 `inbox.mainAttention` 行。一次只消费 marker、不推进水位的 Agent 读取，存的是「只有 marker」的 inbox。`repairLegacyMainStreamRead` 无法把这条当前格式的记录与 Attention 之前的旧凭据区分开，于是给它补了一行 Attention；`validateOperation`（`:3212`）随后按当前格式重新推导出 `advances === false`，期待「只有 marker」的 inbox，两者不符，抛 `invalid Main stream read receipt`。构造函数会 replay 并 validate，因此之后每次启动 Host 都失败。

**复现（实测）：** Agent 在 follow 之前被 Human 在 Main stream @（seq 7）→ `team_attention projectRef follow`（start 8，readThrough 7）→ `team_thread read projectRef`（默认 readThrough = head 7）。读取提交成功（消费 1 个 marker，`advances=false`），随后 `new AgentTeamLedger(table, …)` 抛错。这条路径就是 `main-stream.spec.ts:376` 已经测过的「先被 mention、再 follow、再读」流程，只是那个测试没有重开账本。

**依据：** 修复回归本身。本工作项的验收缝 9 要求「重放校验覆盖迁移后的持久表示」；上一轮修复（`7558dfd`）解决了旧账本打不开，却让新写入的合法记录也打不开。

**最小修复：** 只在当前构建本该写出一行时才修——先算 `this.prepareMainReadFrom(projection, memberId, projectRef, readThroughSequence)`，`!prepared.advances` 时直接 `return operation`。这同时覆盖「readThrough 低于 Attention 起点」的旧部分读取。

---

### major — 非 owner 的 Main stream follower 永远收不到唤醒

**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:2708-2739`（`affectedMembersOf`）

**现象：** 普通 Main 工作的唤醒名单来自 Project owner（`:2731-2737`）、发送者和 Main marker。非 owner Member 的 `mainAttention` 行不出现在名单的任何来源里，而 `touchedThreadRefs` 对 `team/main-message-posted` 不返回 Thread。结果是 follower 的 `standing.unreadCount` 在涨，Host 却从未对它调用 `notifyMember`。

**复现（Host 级实测）：** 非 owner Member follow Project Main → Human 发一条 Main 消息，follower `unreadCount: 1`、唤醒调用 0 次；Human 开一个 discussion，`unreadCount: 2`、唤醒 0 次。反向同样断裂：follower 发言时 `affectedMembersOf` 只返回 `["member:f1"]`，Human owner 不在名单里（Human 的 Main 未读靠派生，本就不在 `projectOwnerIds` 中）。

**依据：** `docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md` 声明 Main stream 普通更新对 Attention 覆盖的读者是 Immediate；`team_attention follow` 的 render 文案是 "Ordinary updates from there will interrupt you"。票据 03 的验收条件要求 owner 与非 owner 在 follow / unfollow / 读取 / **唤醒**上对称。

**最小修复：** 对每个追加 Main source 的操作（`team/main-message-posted`、discussion 形态的 `team/thread-started`、`team/project-owner-added/removed`），把该 Project 下持有 Main attention 行、且不是发送者的 Member 加入名单。**必须先做下一条 membership 门禁**，否则这会把 Main 内容投给非成员。

---

### major — Main stream Attention 的 follow/status 与 Main inbox 行没有 Project 成员门禁

**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:1756-1762`（`writeMainAttention`）、`:1861-1872`（`mainAttentionStatus`）、`:2014-2031`（`mainInboxItems`）、`:1400-1408`（`mainNotificationFacts`）

**现象：** `writeMainAttention` 只校验 Workspace（`assertActorForWorkspace` + `requireActiveProject`），而 `postMainMessage`、`readMainStream`、`mainStreamHistory` 都会调 `requireProjectMemberActor`。Thread 的 inbox 循环有成员门禁（`:1910`），Main 的循环没有。

**复现（实测）：** 一个参与 Workspace 但不属于该 Project 的 Member `changeAttention(projectRef, follow)` 成功提交。随后 `memberInbox` 返回一行 Main，`previewText` 是 Project 消息正文的首行（实测取到 `secret project talk`），而 `mainStreamHistory` 对同一个 Member 抛 `not_project_member`。也就是说：读全文被拒，摘要照样泄露。`team_attention projectRef` 让这成为模型的常规动作。

**依据：** DESIGN「参与与可见性仍由现有权限模型决定」；`docs/AGENTS.md`「Source and tests define implementation behavior」。

**最小修复：** `writeMainAttention` 与 `mainAttentionStatus` 加 `this.requireProjectMemberActor(actor, project.projectRef)`；`mainInboxItems` 与 `mainNotificationFacts` 镜像 Thread 循环的 `isProjectMember` 过滤。**重放校验保持在 `participatesInProjectWorkspaceFrom`**，否则后来被移除成员的历史 follow 无法重放。

---

### major — owner 授权覆盖已存在的 follow 行，静默清掉未读

**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:890-894`（写入）与 `:2925-2927`（校验）

**现象：** `team/project-owner-added` 无条件把 `startMainAttention(member, project, grantSeq)` 放进 delta，替换掉已有行，`readThroughSequence` 被压成 `grantSeq - 1`。

**复现（实测）：** Member follow Main（watermark 1）→ Human 发两条普通更新（unread 2）→ Human 授予 owner 身份，该 Member 的普通未读在没有读取的情况下归 0，存储行的 `readThroughSequence` 跳到授权点。这与「撤回 owner 保留这一行」的对称性相反，也与 `project-owners.spec.ts:107` 的注释「Attention 属于 Member 自己」相反。

**依据：** DESIGN「身份撤销不自动收回既有 Attention：此时持续关注可能已经成为 Member 自己的选择」。同一个问题在 Thread 侧不存在——`followAttention` 会拒绝重复建行。

**最小修复：** 仅在 `mainAttentionForFrom(projection, memberId, projectRef) === undefined` 时才铸授权行，并在 `validateOperation` 的 `grantedMainAttention` 镜像该条件。本构建已写出的账本含覆盖行为，因此校验需同时接受两种形状，或补一条修复。

---

### minor — Human 的 Main stream unfollow 提交成功但什么都不做

**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:1776-1790`、`:4684-4689`

**现象：** `humanMainAttentionFrom` 对存在的 Project 总是返回一行，所以 unfollow 分支写下 `removed: []` 并回一个 receipt、不带 `attention`。`mainAttentionStatus` 与 `standing.following` 仍为 true，普通未读继续流动。用新的 requestId 重复 unfollow 可以无限次提交；follow 则被「already following」拒绝。

**复现（实测）：** unfollow 提交成功 → 状态仍返回 `attention` → 第二次 unfollow 又提交成功 → follow 被拒。通过公开的 `@Remote('changeAttention')` 可达。派生形式满足「默认 follow」这一条（从 `createdAtSequence` 起算、重放确定），但让 unfollow 不可能，且账本报告成功而不是拒绝请求。

**最小修复：** 直接拒绝 Human 的 Main stream unfollow（派生注意力无法结束），或存一个显式 tombstone。当前 Web Client 与 Agent 工具都没有这条路径，属于潜伏缺陷。

---

### minor — 离开 Workspace 不再结束 Main stream Attention

**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:3839-3849`（apply 分支）

**现象：** `team/member-workspace-left` 删除 Project memberships 与 owners，但不碰 `mainAttention`。对比 `removeMemberThreadInboxFrom`（`:4590`）会清掉 Thread Attention 与 Main marker。旧代码在这里删 `mainWatermarks`。

**复现（实测）：** Member 在加入的 Workspace 里 follow Main → 离开 → 期间有新消息 → 重新加入，仍是 `following: true`，且离开期间的消息被算成未读。

**依据：** `docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md:53`（中英同）声明「离开 Workspace、移除和归档会收回这一行，与 Thread Attention 相同」；票据 04 的实施说明同样写「member-workspace-left 同样收回」。代码与票据自己的说明不符，也与 Thread 侧不对称。归档同理（`team/project-archived` 的 `projectArchivalInboxFrom` 清 Thread Attention，不清 Main attention 行）。

**最小修复：** 要么在 apply 分支删掉该 Workspace 下各 Project 的 Main attention 行，要么改文档与票据说明。二者只能改一边；建议按 DESIGN「身份变化不动既有 Attention」的原则改文档——但 Thread 侧的不对称要一并说明。

---

### minor — 通知预算溢出的事实被标记为已覆盖，之后不再触发

**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/index.ts:2810`（`beginInboxDelivery(plan)`）、`:2927`（`slice(0, 8)`）、`packages/agent-team/src/inbox-delivery.ts:49-55`

**现象：** 渲染仍有界（8 段 + 字符预算），但 `covered` 签名覆盖**全部**未读事实，包括文本里被省略的那些。threshold 档移除后，没有任何机制再把未渲染 Thread 的普通更新挡在 `covered` 之外（原先的 `recordedPlan` 会把未渲染 Thread 的 `summarizedThrough` 压住）。

**具体场景：** 一个 owner follow 了 9 个 Thread，各有 1 条普通更新；通知渲染 8 个、覆盖 9 个，于是被丢下的那个 Thread 的更新不会自己触发一次通知，除非之后有别的事实改变签名。

**依据：** 票据 01 验收条件「取消 threshold 不破坏有界合并」；票据 02「同一批未读不重复唤醒」与「唤醒失败能重试」两条都依赖 `covered` 语义准确。

**最小修复：** 从**实际渲染**的事实推导 `covered`，或让溢出的事实保持未覆盖。

---

### minor — `changeAttention` 同时收到两个 scope 时静默择一

**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:1713-1719`、`:6015-6029`

**现象：** 新请求同时带 `projectRef` 与 `threadRef` 时忽略 `threadRef`，follow Main stream。若该 requestId 下已提交过一次 Thread follow，同样的形状会被静默按存储的 Thread 结果应答（`projectRef` 被忽略），于是同一请求形状依提交历史表示两个不同 scope。

**依据：** 工具层拒绝两个 ref 同时出现，Host 层不拒绝；`Remote` 是公开入口。

**最小修复：** 在 fresh 与 replay 两条路径上，`projectRef` 与 `threadRef`/`taskRef` 同时出现即抛错。

---

### minor — 票据 05 的「自动 follow 说明来源」未实现，票据自身已记录

## 追加修复（2026-10-28 晚，来源字段）

第一轮修完后做了 source 字段（`23ed8ee`、`0a19c52`），又跑一轮只读评审，发现三个 blocker，已修（`3fb6bed`、`8a23163`）：

1. **类型检查其实没过**：`withDefault` 的联合类型映射推成联合数组，赋不回 `readonly AgentTeamThreadAttention[]`。我第一轮用 `grep -c "error TS"` 数到 0，是因为错误以 `TypertAnalysisError` 形式从 typert 生成器抛出，不是 `tsc` 行——度量方式错了，不是检查过了。**教训：`npm run typecheck` 要看退出码和完整输出，不能 grep 计数。**
2. **`team_task` 输出 schema 没声明 `source`**，而 `execute` 返回它，`additionalProperties: false` 直接抛 `ToolOutputError`——正好打在这个功能要覆盖的 claim 路径上。被 `member-lifecycle-core.spec.ts` 的真实集成测试抓住。渲染测试抓不到，因为 `renderText` 绕过 schema 校验。
3. **旧账本打不开**：三个校验器（owner grant / claim / task-changed）仍完整比较 source，而 `repairLegacyAttentionSource` 只补一个笼统默认值。

第 3 条的修法改变了设计：不再「按规则版本猜默认值 + 校验时剥掉 source」，改成**从 operation 种类推导真实 source**（grant → `project-owner`，claim → `claim`，thread-started → `thread-author`，transfer/reopen → `accountable`）。这样校验可以保持严格，`sourcelessDelta` 和 `withSource` 两个补丁全部删除——它们一个是过度放行，一个是与 repair 不一致的第二套默认值。

评审还指出 v1 段不全是 mention（v1 也能显式 follow 和 claim），这正是「按版本猜」错的根源；改成按 operation 推导后这个问题自然消失。

2

12	## Findings
13	
14	### blocker — Main stream 读取回放校验拒绝当前格式的记录，账本无法重开
15	
16	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:6292`（`repairLegacyMainStreamRead`），入口 `:6255`
17	
18	**现象：** `prepareMainReadFrom` 只在读取真正推进 watermark 时才写 `inbox.mainAttention` 行。一次只消费 marker、不推进水位的 Agent 读取，存的是「只有 marker」的 inbox。`repairLegacyMainStreamRead` 无法把这条当前格式的记录与 Attention 之前的旧凭据区分开，于是给它补了一行 Attention；`validateOperation`（`:3212`）随后按当前格式重新推导出 `advances === false`，期待「只有 marker」的 inbox，两者不符，抛 `invalid Main stream read receipt`。构造函数会 replay 并 validate，因此之后每次启动 Host 都失败。
19	
20	**复现（实测）：** Agent 在 follow 之前被 Human 在 Main stream @（seq 7）→ `team_attention projectRef follow`（start 8，readThrough 7）→ `team_thread read projectRef`（默认 readThrough = head 7）。读取提交成功（消费 1 个 marker，`advances=false`），随后 `new AgentTeamLedger(table, …)` 抛错。这条路径就是 `main-stream.spec.ts:376` 已经测过的「先被 mention、再 follow、再读」流程，只是那个测试没有重开账本。
21	
22	**依据：** 修复回归本身。本工作项的验收缝 9 要求「重放校验覆盖迁移后的持久表示」；上一轮修复（`7558dfd`）解决了旧账本打不开，却让新写入的合法记录也打不开。
23	
24	**最小修复：** 只在当前构建本该写出一行时才修——先算 `this.prepareMainReadFrom(projection, memberId, projectRef, readThroughSequence)`，`!prepared.advances` 时直接 `return operation`。这同时覆盖「readThrough 低于 Attention 起点」的旧部分读取。
25	
26	---
27	
28	### major — 非 owner 的 Main stream follower 永远收不到唤醒
29	
30	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:2708-2739`（`affectedMembersOf`）
31	
32	**现象：** 普通 Main 工作的唤醒名单来自 Project owner（`:2731-2737`）、发送者和 Main marker。非 owner Member 的 `mainAttention` 行不出现在名单的任何来源里，而 `touchedThreadRefs` 对 `team/main-message-posted` 不返回 Thread。结果是 follower 的 `standing.unreadCount` 在涨，Host 却从未对它调用 `notifyMember`。
33	
34	**复现（Host 级实测）：** 非 owner Member follow Project Main → Human 发一条 Main 消息，follower `unreadCount: 1`、唤醒调用 0 次；Human 开一个 discussion，`unreadCount: 2`、唤醒 0 次。反向同样断裂：follower 发言时 `affectedMembersOf` 只返回 `["member:f1"]`，Human owner 不在名单里（Human 的 Main 未读靠派生，本就不在 `projectOwnerIds` 中）。
35	
36	**依据：** `docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md` 声明 Main stream 普通更新对 Attention 覆盖的读者是 Immediate；`team_attention follow` 的 render 文案是 "Ordinary updates from there will interrupt you"。票据 03 的验收条件要求 owner 与非 owner 在 follow / unfollow / 读取 / **唤醒**上对称。
37	
38	**最小修复：** 对每个追加 Main source 的操作（`team/main-message-posted`、discussion 形态的 `team/thread-started`、`team/project-owner-added/removed`），把该 Project 下持有 Main attention 行、且不是发送者的 Member 加入名单。**必须先做下一条 membership 门禁**，否则这会把 Main 内容投给非成员。
39	
40	---
41	
42	### major — Main stream Attention 的 follow/status 与 Main inbox 行没有 Project 成员门禁
43	
44	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:1756-1762`（`writeMainAttention`）、`:1861-1872`（`mainAttentionStatus`）、`:2014-2031`（`mainInboxItems`）、`:1400-1408`（`mainNotificationFacts`）
45	
46	**现象：** `writeMainAttention` 只校验 Workspace（`assertActorForWorkspace` + `requireActiveProject`），而 `postMainMessage`、`readMainStream`、`mainStreamHistory` 都会调 `requireProjectMemberActor`。Thread 的 inbox 循环有成员门禁（`:1910`），Main 的循环没有。
47	
48	**复现（实测）：** 一个参与 Workspace 但不属于该 Project 的 Member `changeAttention(projectRef, follow)` 成功提交。随后 `memberInbox` 返回一行 Main，`previewText` 是 Project 消息正文的首行（实测取到 `secret project talk`），而 `mainStreamHistory` 对同一个 Member 抛 `not_project_member`。也就是说：读全文被拒，摘要照样泄露。`team_attention projectRef` 让这成为模型的常规动作。
49	
50	**依据：** DESIGN「参与与可见性仍由现有权限模型决定」；`docs/AGENTS.md`「Source and tests define implementation behavior」。
51	
52	**最小修复：** `writeMainAttention` 与 `mainAttentionStatus` 加 `this.requireProjectMemberActor(actor, project.projectRef)`；`mainInboxItems` 与 `mainNotificationFacts` 镜像 Thread 循环的 `isProjectMember` 过滤。**重放校验保持在 `participatesInProjectWorkspaceFrom`**，否则后来被移除成员的历史 follow 无法重放。
53	
54	---

56	### major — owner 授权覆盖已存在的 follow 行，静默清掉未读
57	
58	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:890-894`（写入）与 `:2925-2927`（校验）
59	
60	**现象：** `team/project-owner-added` 无条件把 `startMainAttention(member, project, grantSeq)` 放进 delta，替换掉已有行，`readThroughSequence` 被压成 `grantSeq - 1`。

62	**复现（实测）：** Member follow Main（watermark 1）→ Human 发两条普通更新（unread 2）→ Human 授予 owner 身份，该 Member 的普通未读在没有读取的情况下归 0，存储行的 `readThroughSequence` 跳到授权点。这与「撤回 owner 保留这一行」的对称性相反，也与 `project-owners.spec.ts:107` 的注释「Attention 属于 Member 自己」相反。
63	
64	**依据：** DESIGN「身份撤销不自动收回既有 Attention：此时持续关注可能已经成为 Member 自己的选择」。同一个问题在 Thread 侧不存在——`followAttention` 会拒绝重复建行。
65	
66	**最小修复：** 仅在 `mainAttentionForFrom(projection, memberId, projectRef) === undefined` 时才铸授权行，并在 `validateOperation` 的 `grantedMainAttention` 镜像该条件。本构建已写出的账本含覆盖行为，因此校验需同时接受两种形状，或补一条修复。

70	### minor — Human 的 Main stream unfollow 提交成功但什么都不做
71	
72	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:1776-1790`、`:4684-4689`
73	
74	**现象：** `humanMainAttentionFrom` 对存在的 Project 总是返回一行，所以 unfollow 分支写下 `removed: []` 并回一个 receipt、不带 `attention`。`mainAttentionStatus` 与 `standing.following` 仍为 true，普通未读继续流动。用新的 requestId 重复 unfollow 可以无限次提交；follow 则被「already following」拒绝。
75	
76	**复现（实测）：** unfollow 提交成功 → 状态仍返回 `attention` → 第二次 unfollow 又提交成功 → follow 被拒。通过公开的 `@Remote('changeAttention')` 可达。派生形式满足「默认 follow」这一条（从 `createdAtSequence` 起算、重放确定），但让 unfollow 不可能，且账本报告成功而不是拒绝请求。
77	
78	**最小修复：** 直接拒绝 Human 的 Main stream unfollow（派生注意力无法结束），或存一个显式 tombstone。当前 Web Client 与 Agent 工具都没有这条路径，属于潜伏缺陷。
79	
80	---
81	
82	### minor — 离开 Workspace 不再结束 Main stream Attention
83	
84	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:3839-3849`（apply 分支）
85	
86	**现象：** `team/member-workspace-left` 删除 Project memberships 与 owners，但不碰 `mainAttention`。对比 `removeMemberThreadInboxFrom`（`:4590`）会清掉 Thread Attention 与 Main marker。旧代码在这里删 `mainWatermarks`。

88	**复现（实测）：** Member 在加入的 Workspace 里 follow Main → 离开 → 期间有新消息 → 重新加入，仍是 `following: true`，且离开期间的消息被算成未读。
89	
90	**依据：** `docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md:53`（中英同）声明「离开 Workspace、移除和归档会收回这一行，与 Thread Attention 相同」；票据 04 的实施说明同样写「member-workspace-left 同样收回」。代码与票据自己的说明不符，也与 Thread 侧不对称。归档同理（`team/project-archived` 的 `projectArchivalInboxFrom` 清 Thread Attention，不清 Main attention 行）。
91	
92	**最小修复：** 要么在 apply 分支删掉该 Workspace 下各 Project 的 Main attention 行，要么改文档与票据说明。二者只能改一边；建议按 DESIGN「身份变化不动既有 Attention」的原则改文档——但 Thread 侧的不对称要一并说明。
93

96	### minor — 通知预算溢出的事实被标记为已覆盖，之后不再触发
97	
98	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/index.ts:2810`（`beginInboxDelivery(plan)`）、`:2927`（`slice(0, 8)`）、`packages/agent-team/src/inbox-delivery.ts:49-55`
99	
100	**现象：** 渲染仍有界（8 段 + 字符预算），但 `covered` 签名覆盖**全部**未读事实，包括文本里被省略的那些。threshold 档移除后，没有任何机制再把未渲染 Thread 的普通更新挡在 `covered` 之外（原先的 `recordedPlan` 会把未渲染 Thread 的 `summarizedThrough` 压住）。
101	
102	**具体场景：** 一个 owner follow 了 9 个 Thread，各有 1 条普通更新；通知渲染 8 个、覆盖 9 个，于是被丢下的那个 Thread 的更新不会自己触发一次通知，除非之后有别的事实改变签名。
103	
104	**依据：** 票据 01 验收条件「取消 threshold 不破坏有界合并」；票据 02「同一批未读不重复唤醒」与「唤醒失败能重试」两条都依赖 `covered` 语义准确。
105	
106	**最小修复：** 从**实际渲染**的事实推导 `covered`，或让溢出的事实保持未覆盖。

110	### minor — `changeAttention` 同时收到两个 scope 时静默择一
111	
112	**位置：** `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts:1713-1719`、`:6015-6029`
113	
114	**现象：** 新请求同时带 `projectRef` 与 `threadRef` 时忽略 `threadRef`，follow Main stream。若该 requestId 下已提交过一次 Thread follow，同样的形状会被静默按存储的 Thread 结果应答（`projectRef` 被忽略），于是同一请求形状依提交历史表示两个不同 scope。
115	
116	**依据：** 工具层拒绝两个 ref 同时出现，Host 层不拒绝；`Remote` 是公开入口。
117	
118	**最小修复：** 在 fresh 与 replay 两条路径上，`projectRef` 与 `threadRef`/`taskRef` 同时出现即抛错。

269	第一轮修完后做了 source 字段（`23ed8ee`、`0a19c52`），又跑一轮只读评审，发现三个 blocker，已修（`3fb6bed`、`8a23163`）：
270	
271	1. **类型检查其实没过**：`withDefault` 的联合类型映射推成联合数组，赋不回 `readonly AgentTeamThreadAttention[]`。我第一轮用 `grep -c "error TS"` 数到 0，是因为错误以 `TypertAnalysisError` 形式从 typert 生成器抛出，不是 `tsc` 行——度量方式错了，不是检查过了。**教训：`npm run typecheck` 要看退出码和完整输出，不能 grep 计数。**
272	2. **`team_task` 输出 schema 没声明 `source`**，而 `execute` 返回它，`additionalProperties: false` 直接抛 `ToolOutputError`——正好打在这个功能要覆盖的 claim 路径上。被 `member-lifecycle-core.spec.ts` 的真实集成测试抓住。渲染测试抓不到，因为 `renderText` 绕过 schema 校验。

275	第 3 条的修法改变了设计：不再「按规则版本猜默认值 + 校验时剥掉 source」，改成**从 operation 种类推导真实 source**（grant → `project-owner`，claim → `claim`，thread-started → `thread-author`，transfer/reopen → `accountable`）。这样校验可以保持严格，`sourcelessDelta` 和 `withSource` 两个补丁全部删除——它们一个是过度放行，一个是与 repair 不一致的第二套默认值。

tool.call hook additional context: Contents of /home/yu/projects/dsh-agent-team/.scratch/AGENTS.md:

# .scratch Work Rules

This subtree holds cross-session work items: design snapshots, research, implementation tickets, prototypes, and acceptance evidence. It is not an implementation or API authority — current behavior is defined by `packages/` source and tests, and maintenance rules by [`../docs/AGENTS.md`](../docs/AGENTS.md). This file only governs how to work here.

## Work-item structure

Each `active/<work>/` is one directory with a short `README.md` as its single continuation entry, covering five items: status, last-checked date, current frontier (who is doing what and what is blocked), completion conditions, and the formal-doc exit.

```
active/<work>/
├── README.md      # continuation entry (the five items above)
├── spec.md        # confirmed decision snapshot — written once discussion converges
├── issues/        # tracer-bullet implementation tickets, one file per ticket
│   ├── 01-<slug>.md
│   └── 02-<slug>.md
├── materials/     # research and external material (keep only what is worth re-reading)
└── validation/    # human-confirmed acceptance evidence (see the development doc)
```

## Ticket discipline

Each `issues/NN-<slug>.md` uses a fixed skeleton, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first):

```markdown
# NN — title

**What to build:** the end-to-end behavior this ticket demonstrably delivers once done (user perspective, not a layered task list)
**Blocked by:** the tickets blocking it, or "None — can start immediately"
**Status:** pending | ready | in-progress | complete

- [ ] acceptance criterion 1
- [ ] acceptance criterion 2
```

- **Vertical slices**: each ticket cuts one narrow, complete path through every layer (schema → API → UI → tests), independently verifiable when done; no horizontal division of labor by layer.
- **Self-contained tickets**: each ticket can start in a new context without reading the whole work-item history. Avoid concrete file paths and code snippets (they go stale); exception: decision-dense fragments from prototypes (state machines, type shapes) may be inlined with their source noted.
- **Frontier workflow**: tickets whose blockers are all done form the frontier and are ready to start; a serial chain runs top to bottom. Tickets that are written but still carry unfinished blockers stay **pending**, so `ready` always means startable now.
- **Wide-refactor exception**: when one mechanical change's blast radius covers the whole repository, do not force it into a tracer bullet — order it as expand–contract: expand first (old and new coexist), migrate in batches, then contract (delete the old form).

## Lifecycle

- **Closing a work item**: close or delete unfinished tickets → move durable conclusions into the `../docs/` maintained documents → delete process material without provenance value → move into `archive/YYYY-MM/`.
- **Archive is history**: archived states and terminology only represent the working context of their time and never override current implementation; do not rewrite archives to match new code.
- **Transient artifacts**: logs, debug screenshots, and downloads go in `local/` or `artifacts/` (gitignored), never into active or archive.

## Version control

- **Active does not enter version history**: while a work item is open, its `active/<work>/` directory is gitignored working material. Force-add it (`git add -f`) only when a reviewer must see it.
- **Archive enters history on close**: when a work item closes, move it into `archive/YYYY-MM/` and amend that move into the commit(s) that deliver the work, so the archive records what actually shipped instead of sitting in a scratch-only commit at the tip.

## Directory index

See [README.md](README.md).

1	import type { AgentTeamProjectRef, AgentTeamThreadReadFact, AgentTeamThreadRef } from './types/entities.ts'
2	import type { AgentTeamInboxItem, AgentTeamInboxReminder, AgentTeamMainTimelineEntry } from './types/requests-results.ts'
3	
4	/**
5	 * Every unread fact interrupts: there is one delivery class. An ordinary Thread
6	 * update reaches a reader only because it follows that Thread, a mention or a
7	 * reply carries a direct marker, and a responsibility Activity or live Task
8	 * reminder arrives through its own marker — so what decides whether ordinary
9	 * work exists at all is Attention, never how fast it travels. No identity
10	 * chooses a slower class here. `covered` is what keeps an unchanged
11	 * rederivation from spending a second attempt on the same durable facts.
12	 */
13	export type InboxDelivery = 'immediate'
14	
15	/** The reader's role in one notice scope, as the notice states it. */
16	export type InboxScopeRole = 'follower' | 'member'
17	
18	export interface InboxThreadUnread {
19	  readonly item: AgentTeamInboxItem
20	  readonly facts: readonly AgentTeamThreadReadFact[]
21	  readonly reminders?: readonly AgentTeamInboxReminder[]
22	}
23	
24	export interface InboxMainUnread {
25	  readonly projectRef: AgentTeamProjectRef
26	  readonly entries: readonly AgentTeamMainTimelineEntry[]
27	}
28	
29	export interface InboxDeliveryInput {
30	  readonly threads: readonly InboxThreadUnread[]
31	  readonly main: readonly InboxMainUnread[]
32	  /** Signature of the immediate facts the last delivery attempt answered. */
33	  readonly covered: string | undefined
34	  /**
35	   * Threads the last notice could not render, so its facts were never delivered.
36	   * Their facts still enter this signature — otherwise an unchanged
37	   * rederivation would look identical to the delivered one — but the facts the
38	   * last attempt actually answered are the ones `covered` may match.
39	   */
40	  readonly undelivered?: readonly AgentTeamThreadRef[] | undefined
41	}
42	
43	export interface InboxThreadPlan {
44	  readonly threadRef: AgentTeamThreadRef
45	  readonly role: InboxScopeRole
46	  readonly delivery: InboxDelivery
47	}
48	
49	export interface InboxDeliveryPlan {
50	  /** Why a notice goes out now, or `undefined` when nothing may interrupt the reader. */
51	  readonly trigger: InboxDelivery | undefined
52	  readonly signature: string
53	  /** The signature the next rederivation compares `covered` against: everything the notice can actually render. */
54	  readonly delivered: string
55	  readonly threads: readonly InboxThreadPlan[]
56	}
57	
58	export function planInboxDelivery(input: InboxDeliveryInput): InboxDeliveryPlan {
59	  const immediate: (string | number)[][] = []
60	  const delivered: (string | number)[][] = []
61	  const threads: InboxThreadPlan[] = []
62	  const undelivered = new Set(input.undelivered ?? [])
63	  for (const { item, facts, reminders = [] } of input.threads) {
64	    const threadRef = item.thread.threadRef
65	    // A reminder is always delivered: it is the whole reason the notice exists
66	    // when the Thread holds no ordinary unread.
67	    if (reminders.length > 0) {
68	      const reminderFacts = [threadRef, 'reminder', ...reminders.map(reminder => `${reminder.kind}:${reminder.baselineSequence}`)]
69	      immediate.push(reminderFacts)
70	      delivered.push(reminderFacts)
71	    }
72	    const now = facts.map(entry => entry.fact.sequence)
73	    if (now.length > 0) immediate.push([threadRef, ...now])
74	    // A Thread the notice cannot render is not delivered by this attempt, so its
75	    // facts are not what `covered` records: an unchanged rederivation still sees
76	    // them as owed and re-attempts instead of standing down.
77	    if (now.length > 0 && !undelivered.has(threadRef)) delivered.push([threadRef, ...now])
78	    threads.push(Object.freeze({ threadRef, role: item.attention === undefined ? 'member' : 'follower', delivery: 'immediate' as const }))
79	  }
80	  for (const { projectRef, entries } of input.main) {
81	    if (entries.length > 0) { immediate.push([projectRef, ...entries.map(entry => entry.sequence)]); delivered.push([projectRef, ...entries.map(entry => entry.sequence)]) }
82	  }
83	  const signature = immediate.length === 0 ? '' : JSON.stringify(immediate)
84	  const covered = delivered.length === 0 ? '' : JSON.stringify(delivered)
85	  const trigger = signature !== '' && covered !== input.covered ? 'immediate' : undefined
86	  return Object.freeze({ trigger, signature, delivered: covered, threads: Object.freeze(threads) })
87	}

1	import type { AgentTeamProjectRef, AgentTeamThreadReadFact, AgentTeamThreadRef } from './types/entities.ts'
2	import type { AgentTeamInboxItem, AgentTeamInboxReminder, AgentTeamMainTimelineEntry } from './types/requests-results.ts'
3	
4	/**
5	 * Every unread fact interrupts: there is one delivery class. An ordinary Thread
6	 * update reaches a reader only because it follows that Thread, a mention or a
7	 * reply carries a direct marker, and a responsibility Activity or live Task
8	 * reminder arrives through its own marker — so what decides whether ordinary
9	 * work exists at all is Attention, never how fast it travels. No identity
10	 * chooses a slower class here. `covered` is what keeps an unchanged
11	 * rederivation from spending a second attempt on the same durable facts.
12	 */
13	export type InboxDelivery = 'immediate'
14	
15	/** The reader's role in one notice scope, as the notice states it. */
16	export type InboxScopeRole = 'follower' | 'member'
17	
18	export interface InboxThreadUnread {
19	  readonly item: AgentTeamInboxItem
20	  readonly facts: readonly AgentTeamThreadReadFact[]
21	  readonly reminders?: readonly AgentTeamInboxReminder[]
22	}
23	
24	export interface InboxMainUnread {
25	  readonly projectRef: AgentTeamProjectRef
26	  readonly entries: readonly AgentTeamMainTimelineEntry[]
27	}
28	
29	export interface InboxDeliveryInput {
30	  readonly threads: readonly InboxThreadUnread[]
31	  readonly main: readonly InboxMainUnread[]
32	  /** Signature of the immediate facts the last delivery attempt answered. */
33	  readonly covered: string | undefined
34	  /**
35	   * Threads the last notice could not render, so its facts were never delivered.
36	   * Their facts still enter this signature — otherwise an unchanged
37	   * rederivation would look identical to the delivered one — but the facts the
38	   * last attempt actually answered are the ones `covered` may match.
39	   */
40	  readonly undelivered?: readonly AgentTeamThreadRef[] | undefined
41	}
42	
43	export interface InboxThreadPlan {
44	  readonly threadRef: AgentTeamThreadRef
45	  readonly role: InboxScopeRole
46	  readonly delivery: InboxDelivery
47	}
48	
49	export interface InboxDeliveryPlan {
50	  /** Why a notice goes out now, or `undefined` when nothing may interrupt the reader. */
51	  readonly trigger: InboxDelivery | undefined
52	  readonly signature: string
53	  /** The signature the next rederivation compares `covered` against: everything the notice can actually render. */
54	  readonly delivered: string
55	  readonly threads: readonly InboxThreadPlan[]
56	}
57	
58	export function planInboxDelivery(input: InboxDeliveryInput): InboxDeliveryPlan {
59	  const immediate: (string | number)[][] = []
60	  const delivered: (string | number)[][] = []
61	  const threads: InboxThreadPlan[] = []
62	  const undelivered = new Set(input.undelivered ?? [])
63	  for (const { item, facts, reminders = [] } of input.threads) {
64	    const threadRef = item.thread.threadRef
65	    // A reminder is always delivered: it is the whole reason the notice exists
66	    // when the Thread holds no ordinary unread.
67	    if (reminders.length > 0) {
68	      const reminderFacts = [threadRef, 'reminder', ...reminders.map(reminder => `${reminder.kind}:${reminder.baselineSequence}`)]
69	      immediate.push(reminderFacts)
70	      delivered.push(reminderFacts)
71	    }
72	    const now = facts.map(entry => entry.fact.sequence)
73	    if (now.length > 0) immediate.push([threadRef, ...now])
74	    // A Thread the notice cannot render is not delivered by this attempt, so its
75	    // facts are not what `covered` records: an unchanged rederivation still sees
76	    // them as owed and re-attempts instead of standing down.
77	    if (now.length > 0 && !undelivered.has(threadRef)) delivered.push([threadRef, ...now])
78	    threads.push(Object.freeze({ threadRef, role: item.attention === undefined ? 'member' : 'follower', delivery: 'immediate' as const }))
79	  }
80	  for (const { projectRef, entries } of input.main) {
81	    if (entries.length > 0) { immediate.push([projectRef, ...entries.map(entry => entry.sequence)]); delivered.push([projectRef, ...entries.map(entry => entry.sequence)]) }
82	  }
83	  const signature = immediate.length === 0 ? '' : JSON.stringify(immediate)
84	  const covered = delivered.length === 0 ? '' : JSON.stringify(delivered)
85	  const trigger = signature !== '' && covered !== input.covered ? 'immediate' : undefined
86	  return Object.freeze({ trigger, signature, delivered: covered, threads: Object.freeze(threads) })
87	}

## deepwiki
DeepWiki MCP provides AI-powered documentation for GitHub repositories.

With a user OAuth token, all devin_* tools act in one organization: without an X-Org-Id header, the first one the user joined. Not found usually means another of their orgs; send X-Org-Id: <org id> to switch.

Available tools:
- read_wiki_structure: Get a list of documentation topics for a repository
- read_wiki_contents: View full documentation about a repository
- ask_wiki_question: Ask any question about a repository's codebase and get an AI-powered answer from its wiki
- list_wiki_repos: List the repositories that have a DeepWiki index (private mode only)
- generate_wiki: Generate a codebase wiki for a repository — only use when explicitly requested by the user (private mode only)
- devin_automation_manage: Manage Devin automations — list, get, create, update, delete, or fetch the trigger event schemas (private mode only)
- devin_billing_tag_manage: Manage Devin billing tags (groupings of Devin sessions for usage tracking) — list, get, create, assign sessions, look up session tags (private mode only)
- devin_blueprint_test: Test a candidate blueprint YAML in an authoring VM: start → run initialize → fix → run initialize again (clean VM) → run maintenance → then persist with update_environment_config (private mode only)
- devin_campaign_manage: Read and publish a bot's campaign documents (plan, readings, status) — get, update, validate (private mode only)
- devin_code_scan_manage: Manage Devin code scans, sometimes referred to as 'security scans' or 'Devin Security Swarm' — list scans, list findings, list profiles, get a profile, create a scan, remediate a finding (private mode only)
- devin_knowledge_manage: Manage Devin knowledge notes and suggestions — list, search, get, create, update, delete notes, view folder structure, list/view/dismiss knowledge suggestions (private mode only)
- devin_mcp_server_manage: Manage org MCP server installations — install (marketplace or custom), update, enable, disable, delete (private mode only)
- devin_oncall_manage: Devin Oncall operations — create and manage Oncall responders (alert, bug report and support request triage), get an Oncall report's current responder membership, page through a responder's open issues, and ingest a dashboard into Oncall knowledge (private mode only)
- devin_playbook_manage: Manage Devin playbooks — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_review_manage: Trigger a Devin Review for a pull request, fetch the latest review status, or fetch a completed review's findings (private mode only)
- devin_schedule_manage: Manage scheduled Devin sessions — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_session_create: Create one or more child Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_interact: Manage a Devin session — get status (one or many sessions, optionally with a short AI summary of each), send messages, sleep/terminate/archive/unarchive, read messages & attachments, manage tags (private mode only)
- devin_session_events: Inspect session events — list summaries, fetch full details, or search event contents (private mode only)
- devin_session_search: Search and filter Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_insights: Per-session cost, message counts and AI analysis (issues, action items, classification) — list, get, generate (private mode only)
- devin_user_list: List the organization's users by membership kind (direct members or IdP-group members) (private mode only)
- devin_list_integrations: List all native integrations and MCP servers with their status and settings URLs (private mode only)
- devin_find_setting: Find Devin webapp settings pages and deep-link URLs for them (private mode only)

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## deepwiki
DeepWiki MCP provides AI-powered documentation for GitHub repositories.

With a user OAuth token, all devin_* tools act in one organization: without an X-Org-Id header, the first one the user joined. Not found usually means another of their orgs; send X-Org-Id: <org id> to switch.

Available tools:
- read_wiki_structure: Get a list of documentation topics for a repository
- read_wiki_contents: View full documentation about a repository
- ask_wiki_question: Ask any question about a repository's codebase and get an AI-powered answer from its wiki
- list_wiki_repos: List the repositories that have a DeepWiki index (private mode only)
- generate_wiki: Generate a codebase wiki for a repository — only use when explicitly requested by the user (private mode only)
- devin_automation_manage: Manage Devin automations — list, get, create, update, delete, or fetch the trigger event schemas (private mode only)
- devin_billing_tag_manage: Manage Devin billing tags (groupings of Devin sessions for usage tracking) — list, get, create, assign sessions, look up session tags (private mode only)
- devin_blueprint_test: Test a candidate blueprint YAML in an authoring VM: start → run initialize → fix → run initialize again (clean VM) → run maintenance → then persist with update_environment_config (private mode only)
- devin_campaign_manage: Read and publish a bot's campaign documents (plan, readings, status) — get, update, validate (private mode only)
- devin_code_scan_manage: Manage Devin code scans, sometimes referred to as 'security scans' or 'Devin Security Swarm' — list scans, list findings, list profiles, get a profile, create a scan, remediate a finding (private mode only)
- devin_knowledge_manage: Manage Devin knowledge notes and suggestions — list, search, get, create, update, delete notes, view folder structure, list/view/dismiss knowledge suggestions (private mode only)
- devin_mcp_server_manage: Manage org MCP server installations — install (marketplace or custom), update, enable, disable, delete (private mode only)
- devin_oncall_manage: Devin Oncall operations — create and manage Oncall responders (alert, bug report and support request triage), get an Oncall report's current responder membership, page through a responder's open issues, and ingest a dashboard into Oncall knowledge (private mode only)
- devin_playbook_manage: Manage Devin playbooks — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_review_manage: Trigger a Devin Review for a pull request, fetch the latest review status, or fetch a completed review's findings (private mode only)
- devin_schedule_manage: Manage scheduled Devin sessions — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_session_create: Create one or more child Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_interact: Manage a Devin session — get status (one or many sessions, optionally with a short AI summary of each), send messages, sleep/terminate/archive/unarchive, read messages & attachments, manage tags (private mode only)
- devin_session_events: Inspect session events — list summaries, fetch full details, or search event contents (private mode only)
- devin_session_search: Search and filter Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_insights: Per-session cost, message counts and AI analysis (issues, action items, classification) — list, get, generate (private mode only)
- devin_user_list: List the organization's users by membership kind (direct members or IdP-group members) (private mode only)
- devin_list_integrations: List all native integrations and MCP servers with their status and settings URLs (private mode only)
- devin_find_setting: Find Devin webapp settings pages and deep-link URLs for them (private mode only)

docs/team-collaboration/tools.md:101:`board` renders the Host's Task board projection: every open Task of the Projects the reader can see, grouped into To do, In progress, and In review, newest activity first, then each Project's five newest finished Tasks. Each row carries the Task ref and number, Project, Thread ref, the Members on live Claims, the reader's relation (`accountable`, `executor`, or `project-owner`), the accountable owner, whether the reader may accept it, a bounded subject, and the last-activity instant.
docs/team-collaboration/tools.zh.md:83:`board` 渲染 Host 的 Task board 投影：读者可见 Project 的全部 open Task，按待处理、进行中、待验收分组、按最新活动排序；再列每个 Project 最近完成的 5 个 Task。每行携带 Task ref 与编号、Project、Thread ref、live Claim 上的 Members、读者与它的关系（`accountable`、`executor` 或 `project-owner`）、负责人、读者是否可验收、有界主题与最新活动时刻。
docs/architecture/host-authority.md:17:- An Attention row carries the `source` that established it: `thread-author`, `claim`, `accountable`, `project-owner`, `mention`, or `self`. It is optional in storage, so rows written before it existed keep their bytes.
docs/architecture/host-authority.md:18:- On load, a missing cause is derived from the operation that wrote the row: an ownership grant reads as `project-owner`, a Claim as `claim`, a Thread start as `thread-author`, a transfer or reopen as `accountable`. A repaired row therefore matches the one the validator re-derives, so every comparison stays exact. Deriving rather than guessing is what keeps the field out of validation — a value that could be inferred two ways would have to be excluded, and an excluded field is one a writer can get wrong without anything noticing.

docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md:6:Attention is durable private state for one Member and Thread: current period start, contiguous read watermark, and what established the period. Creating a Thread (its author follows), creating a Task Claim, being named accountable — by a transfer, a promotion, or a reopen — or explicitly following starts it; a rules-version-1 mention started it too, which is the only source version 2 no longer produces. Taskless Threads can be unfollowed directly; taskful Threads require no active Claim. Unfollow ends the period and discards its unread work; a later follow starts at the current tail.
docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md:10:While active, other Members' Messages—and taskful Claim and Task resolution Activities—become ordinary unread. Mentions create durable direct markers. The sender's own mutation is not unread. Promotion creates a `promote` Activity for current followers. Follow/unfollow/read are private and do not advance Thread revision. Close ends Attention; reopen does not restore old periods, but a new reopen restores the accountable's current follow unless the accountable is the actor or already follows.
docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md:20:Both Thread faces render one follow control: its pressed state is read from the Host's current follower set asked about the Human's own Member id, the write goes through the Human `changeAttention` Remote, and the control never optimistically flips, so a refused write leaves the previous standing on screen with its failure beside the control. The Human-only follow/unfollow observations themselves are not rendered as history.
docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md:55:Withdrawing Project ownership is not an unfollow: the Member keeps the Main stream Attention it was granted and keeps receiving ordinary updates until it reads or unfollows. Only the owner privilege is gone. Member removal and archival end the row, the same as Thread Attention; leaving a Workspace and archiving the Project do not, so a Member that returns finds its Attention where it left it.
docs/team-collaboration/tools.md:42:4. active Claims only — the current collision surface, one line per Claim (claim ref, owner, direction);
docs/team-collaboration/tools.md:55:`team_attention` answers one question — am I following this Thread or this Project's Main stream, and should I be? `status` reports the current state and changes nothing; `follow` starts receiving ordinary updates from there; `unfollow` stops them. All three take the address and the routing Workspace. `threadRef` is primary for a Thread, with `taskRef` as the compatibility alias, and `projectRef` addresses the Main stream instead — exactly one of the three, and a call carrying both a Thread and a `projectRef` is refused rather than silently preferring one.
docs/team-collaboration/tools.md:61:Every result states the consequence its verb alone does not carry. Following means ordinary updates from there interrupt you. Unfollowing means they stop, while a mention, a reply to you, and a responsibility event still reach you — and unfollowing releases no Claim and drops no Task you are accountable for, so it is a subscription change rather than a withdrawal from the work. An active Claim on the Task refuses the Thread unfollow until it is done or released. [Attention and messaging](attention-and-messaging.md) owns the rows themselves.
docs/team-collaboration/tools.md:111:`list`, `claim`, `done`, and `release` manage only the Agent's own Direction Claims on real Tasks. Taskless Threads have no Claim mutation. A Direction is one sentence describing the Agent's angle; plans and acceptance checklists belong in Thread messages. A successful Claim starts Attention. `list` renders the Task/Thread identity with the active collision surface — active Claims only, or an explicit none — and no write token, because a current `team_thread read` remains the required mutation basis.

content.content:
---
name: team-domain-model
description: Reference for how a Project, its owners and members, the Main stream, Threads, Tasks, and notifications work in this Team. Read this skill when you are unsure who may start a discussion or Task, claim, accept, close, reopen, or transfer one; whether a mention, a reply, or an ordinary message will interrupt someone; whether something belongs in the Main stream, a Thread, or a DM; when to look at the board or Inbox; or after a rejection such as project_owner_required, not_project_member, main_unread_required, unread_required, stale_revision, self_acceptance_forbidden, or accountable_owner_required. Stable rules only, never current state.
---

# Team Domain Model

Stable rules for acting in a Project. Current state comes from your context and the Team tools, never from this skill; the Host enforces every rule below, and this text only helps you avoid rejections.

## Roles and permissions

- **Human**: always an owner of every Project. May accept, close, reopen, or take back any Task at any time, including accepting early. Cannot be DMed and does not Claim.
- **Project owner**: the Human, plus any Agents the Human names. Your context lists the Projects you own.
- **Project member**: owners, anyone mentioned in the Project, anyone who has spoken, claimed, or followed there, and legacy explicit members — limited to Members still in the Workspace and not archived or inactive.
- **Accountable**: the one owner who drives a Task to acceptance — an Agent Project owner or the Human. An Agent owner creating a Task is accountable by default; a Human names one or leaves it to the Human. It either verifies the work or transfers it.

| Action | Who | Otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read a Project, post, reply | Project member | `not_project_member` |
| `team_message` start (discussion or Task) | Project owner | `project_owner_required` |
| Promote a discussion to a Task (`team_task` promote) | Human, Project owner | `project_owner_required` |
| `team_task` claim | Agent Project member, open Task | rejected |
| `team_task` done / release | Only the Claim's owner | `claim_owned_by_another` |
| `team_task` accept | Human; a Project owner who never claimed it, only at in_review | `self_acceptance_forbidden` |
| `team_task` close / reopen / transfer | Human, current accountable | `accountable_owner_required` |

If you are not an owner and something needs a discussion or Task, post in the Main stream and mention an owner. Once a Task is accepted or closed, Claim changes are refused; a closed Task also refuses replies until reopened.

## Main stream and Threads

- The **Main stream** is the Project's open conversation: questions, heads-up, requests. It has no Task, Claim, or write token, and ordinary posts never create a Thread. Discussions and Tasks appear in it as cards. It has its own Attention: `team_attention` with `projectRef` follows or unfollows it.
- A **Thread** is one standing question (discussion) or one piece of work (Task), opened by an owner with its first message. Work, decisions, and evidence go there.
- A **Task** is a Thread with a work status derived from its Claims: todo (none), in_progress (a Claim is active), in_review (none active, one done). An accept (done) or close overrides it.
- **DM** (`team_dm`): a brief private question to one enabled Agent in your Workspace, or detailed evidence for one peer. Never task work or decisions; past about 3 exchanges, move to a Thread. Recorded even if the recipient cannot be woken; never resend blindly.
- `@all` has no special meaning; it is plain text. Mention each Member as `@Handle`.

## Mention, reply, ordinary message

| You write | Who is notified | Immediate? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Handle` in the body | that Member, once, for that Message only | yes |
| Reply with `replyToMessageRef` | the author of that Message, like a mention | yes |
| Ordinary Thread message | Thread followers | immediately |
| Main stream message | the Project's other owners | yes |
| New discussion | other owners, like a Main stream post | yes |
| New Task | not other owners; they find it on the board | no |

- A mention or reply never makes someone follow and never delivers earlier messages; whoever enters cold reads `team_thread` history first.
- Following controls ordinary updates only: starting a Thread or a successful Claim follows it, replying does not. Owning a Project follows its Main stream from the grant, not its Threads. `team_attention` follows or unfollows either face and reads nothing; unfollowing stops ordinary updates only.
- An ordinary message does not notify the author you answer: when you answer an owner or report a result, mention them or link the reply.

## Where to look

- **Inbox** (`team_inbox`): your own unread, split into ordinary unread and direct notices (mentions, linked replies, responsibility events). Read items with `team_thread`; the Main stream is read with `projectRef`.
- **Board** (`team_task board`): every open Task with its status, accountable owner, and who is on it, plus recently finished work, whether or not you have unread; `mine` narrows to what you are accountable for or execute. Look before claiming, and when a new Task matters.
- `team_view` is also the address book for Projects, Members, and recent Threads.

## Task lifecycle

1. An owner starts a Task (`kind: task`, optionally naming `accountable` and `sourceThreadRefs`) or promotes a discussion in place; a derived Task shows its card in those Threads, an in-place promotion records no source.
2. An Agent member announces in the Thread and claims one Direction (`team_task claim`), making it in_progress.
3. The Claim holder reports verification in the Thread, then marks its own Claim `done`. With no active Claim and one done, the Task is in_review.
4. `accept` verifies finished work: the Human any time, an Agent Project owner only at in_review and only if it never claimed the Task — released Claims count, and reopening does not clear that. `close` ends it unaccepted, `reopen` returns it to open work, and `transfer` hands responsibility on without moving Claims. Report, mention whoever waits, close out.
5. `release` abandons your Claim; an unclaimed Task stays open.

## Rejections and recovery

| Code | Meaning | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_owner_required` | Only an owner starts or promotes a Thread | `post` in the Main stream and mention an owner |
| `not_project_member` | You are not a member of that Project | Choose a Project from `team_view`, or ask the Human or an owner to mention you |
| `main_unread_required` | Unread Main stream entries (ordinary unread your Attention covers, or any mention) | `team_thread read` with `projectRef`, then post |
| `unread_required` | Unread facts in the Thread | `team_thread read` until drained, reconsider, then write |
| `stale_revision` | The Thread moved since your token | Read again; use the new token |
| `missing_write_token` | No token supplied | Drain with a read, or reuse your last committed mutation's token |
| `claim_owned_by_another` | Not your Claim | `team_task list`, change only your own |
| `self_acceptance_forbidden` | You claimed this Task, so you cannot verify it | Ask the Human, or `transfer` it to an owner who never claimed it |
| `accountable_owner_required` | Only the accountable or the Human | Ask them to act, or to transfer it to you |
| `reply_target_unknown` | `replyToMessageRef` is not in this Thread or Main stream | Copy a messageRef from a read or notice |
| `unknown_ref`, `ambiguous_ref` | Bad or short ref | Reuse the full ref |
| `workspace_required`, `workspace_not_participating` | Workspace unclear | Pass `workspace` from `team_view` |

A rejection supplies no write basis: read the named Thread or Main stream, reconsider, then write again.
